[I], the lead's ruling on lane 1.11r's answer (docs/research/2026-11-16-1861-gaps.md, Part F): 30 days from a call to a sitting quorum. In 1861 the proclamation of 15 April took 80 days to a quorum on 4 July; the shortest feasible lag is not on record. Comparisons: the Confederate Provisional Congress, 17 days (12 to 29 April 1861); Tyler's call of 1841, 75 days; Cleveland's of 1893, 38 days; the Constitution sets no minimum notice. It sits 34 days, as the 1861 session did [I]. Lane 1.14 calibrates
